assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity opened moire quantum matter, a new tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons. It fits the committee's interest in new states of matter in materials, and theory and experiment meet unusually cleanly.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. Within the supplied names this is a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other experimental groups and theorists may have claims that the supplied credit does not capture.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated insulators and superconductivity, and the field is large and still growing. The origin of the superconductivity is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid. Recognition is timely, although a few more years of consolidation would not hurt.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene is not settled.
Credit for the experimental discovery may be seen as extending beyond a single group; I have not verified details of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators introduced a new classification of electronic phases by band topology, with protected edge and surface states. It is a conceptually deep and lasting change of how we understand quantum matter, and is also materially real and spectroscopically verified (for example by ARPES).
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall insulator, and Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied names give a workable theory-plus-experiment trio, but other key contributors (for example for the HgTe prediction and for 3D topological insulators) are not in the credited list, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed by independent experiments over nearly two decades, and the topological-materials concept has spread widely. Recognition is somewhat overdue, but the 2016 prize on topological phases partly overlaps and may be argued to cover part of the territory.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and phases of matter.
The list omits some people usually associated with the HgTe prediction and 3D topological insulators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello ab initio molecular dynamics unified density functional theory and dynamics, allowing first-principles simulation of liquids, chemical reactions and defects. It is one of the most widely used computational methods in condensed-matter physics, chemistry and materials science. As a theorist in this area, I regard its impact as very large and the method as clear and original.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is the unambiguous origin and the two-person credit is clean. Others developed later extensions (such as Born-Oppenheimer variants), but the original credit is not much in doubt.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of heavy use give the strongest confirmation. Timing is long overdue rather than premature. The main doubt is whether the committee views a computational method as a discovery or invention of the right kind for the physics prize, given the 1998 chemistry prize for DFT and the 2013 chemistry prize for multiscale modelling.
uncertainties: Whether the Physics prize would be seen as overlapping chemistry's recognition of computational methods.
Contribution of other methodological developments to the practical success of ab initio dynamics is not assessed here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration of electron lenses enabled routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atomic structure in materials. This is a clear instrumentation invention with enormous impact on condensed-matter and materials physics, and ties well to spectroscopy that tests theory such as electronic-structure calculations.
assessment.attribution: Rose (theory of the corrector), Haider (implementation in TEM) and Urban (demonstration in the instrument and application to materials) form a clean three-person configuration frequently discussed as the natural one. Others, such as Krivanek in STEM correction, could also claim credit; I do not verify this.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with widespread commercial deployment and independent confirmation. The 1986 prize for the electron microscope itself is a possible precedent for instrument prizes, but is also a reminder that there is little novelty of fundamental physics to recognise.
uncertainties: Whether instrument-oriented recognition is competitive against discovery-based candidates this year.
Credit may extend to STEM aberration correction developers outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors and a large body of work on unconventional pairing, magnetism and nematicity. It is important physics and a genuine surprise to a community that thought iron-based magnets would be hostile to superconductivity.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the discovery in LaFeAsO(F), and the rapid extension to higher Tc by Chinese groups (Chen, Zhao and others) was decisive for the field's growth. A single-laureate or a two-or-three-person configuration is possible; I propose Hosono alone as the clear originator, with the follow-up credit disputed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and with great speed; transition temperatures are not higher than cuprates, and the pairing mechanism is not settled. The impact is large, but the lack of application and the unresolved mechanism lower my confidence on timing.
uncertainties: How much weight to give the rapid Chinese follow-up versus the original discovery is a judgement the supplied credit does not resolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition in a controlled system, giving a quantum simulator for many-body physics. It is a quantum-materials bridge: theory-defined models tested in clean experiments.
assessment.attribution: Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger did the key experiments (Greiner's Mott transition work with Bloch and Hänsch; Esslinger's fermionic Hubbard and Mott work). Zoller, the main theorist, is also credited, and any configuration would need to omit one of four strong contributors, which is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation worldwide, and the research is maturing into quantitative simulation. The 2001 and 2012 prizes on atomic physics partly relate, and the allocation among four names is a real difficulty.
uncertainties: Four-way credit problem; Zoller's theory role is omitted in my proposed set.
Overlap with earlier BEC and cold-atom prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of record precision, have taken timekeeping to the 10^-18 level and opened new tests of fundamental physics and geodesy. A clear and very important invention that gives measurable quantitative improvements.
assessment.attribution: Katori's 2003 magic-wavelength proposal and first lattice clock, and Ye's later precision realisations, make a two-person configuration natural. Hall and Hänsch were already recognised in 2005 for frequency combs which Ye's group uses, and other clock groups (for example ion clocks) would argue for credit, but those are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced by numerous labs; redefinition of the second is under discussion, which would make recognition especially timely. This is a little outside my own area, so I defer partly to colleagues in atomic physics.
uncertainties: Possible competing credit for ion clocks and for people not on this list.
I am less expert in atomic physics than in condensed matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity in organic Bechgaard salts opened the study of molecular conductors and low-dimensional correlated electron physics, including spin-density waves, Luttinger-liquid behaviour and unconventional superconductivity. It is a historically important finding that shaped ideas on strongly correlated materials.
assessment.attribution: Bechgaard synthesised the salts, and Jérome and colleagues discovered superconductivity in (TMTSF)2PF6 in 1980; Saito's later work extended the field to BEDT-TTF superconductors. A three-person configuration is plausible but the roles and the exact attribution of the original collaboration are partly uncertain to me.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent confirmation. The risk is that the discovery is now old and the field's visibility has declined relative to newer superconductors, which weakens the case for a prize now.
uncertainties: Credit among the discovery collaboration, which included more people than the three names, is uncertain.
Lower current visibility reduces urgency compared with active fields.
